quests.instruction: A farmer trims a thick, fluffy coat off this animal so it can be spun into yarn. Which animal is it?
quests.hint: Think about what a warm hat or scarf is knitted from.
quests.explanation: Sheep grow thick woolly coats. Once a year a farmer shears the wool off, and it is spun into yarn for hats, socks and scarves.
quests.funFact: A sheep's pupils are shaped like horizontal rectangles, which helps it see almost all the way around the field.
quests.question: Sheep

quests.instruction: Every morning, a farmer checks the nest boxes and finds fresh eggs. Who laid them?
quests.hint: A nest, some straw and a lot of clucking are clues.
quests.explanation: Hens lay eggs, and a healthy hen can lay about one egg a day. Farmers collect them so people can eat them.
quests.funFact: A mother hen gently turns her eggs many times a day so the chick inside stays evenly warm.
quests.question: Chicken

quests.instruction: The milk you pour on your cereal comes from which farm animal?
quests.hint: Farmers collect it from this animal twice a day in a big barn.
quests.explanation: A mother cow makes milk to feed her calf, and dairy farms collect some of the extra for people to drink.
quests.funFact: A cow chews her food twice: first a quick bite, then she brings it back up later and chews it again.
quests.question: Cow

quests.instruction: Curled up on the sofa, one pet makes a soft rumbling sound. Who is it?
quests.hint: The sound comes from deep in its throat when it feels comfy.
quests.explanation: Cats purr when they feel calm and safe. Some also purr to comfort themselves when they are worried.
quests.funFact: Cats cannot taste sweet things. They are missing the taste sensor that detects sugar.
quests.question: Cat

quests.instruction: Throw the ball and this pet zooms off, then brings it back wagging its tail. Which pet?
quests.hint: Listen for a happy swishing tail when you walk through the door.
quests.explanation: Dogs wag their tails when they feel excited, and chasing things comes naturally to many dogs.
quests.funFact: A dog's nose print is one of a kind, a bit like your fingerprint.
quests.question: Dog

quests.instruction: Long ears, a twitchy nose and springy back legs. Which pet is this?
quests.hint: Its back legs are much stronger than its front legs.
quests.explanation: Rabbits hop on powerful back legs, and their tall ears swivel to catch sounds from every side.
quests.funFact: A rabbit's front teeth never stop growing, so chewing keeps them from getting too long.
quests.question: Rabbit

quests.instruction: Which animal is the biggest animal walking on land?
quests.hint: It is taller than most doorways and as heavy as several cars.
quests.explanation: African elephants are the largest land animals. A big male can weigh several tonnes.
quests.funFact: An elephant can pick up a single peanut with its trunk, and also lift a heavy log.
quests.question: Elephant

quests.instruction: Which animal is the tallest in the world?
quests.hint: It can nibble leaves from the tops of trees.
quests.explanation: Giraffes can grow about five metres tall, so they eat leaves that other animals can't reach.
quests.funFact: A giraffe has seven neck bones, just like you. Each one is just much, much longer.
quests.question: Giraffe

quests.instruction: This wild animal has black and white stripes all over. Which one?
quests.hint: It looks a bit like a horse that is wearing pyjamas.
quests.explanation: Zebras are wild relatives of horses. Their stripes may help keep biting flies away.
quests.funFact: No two zebras have exactly the same stripes.
quests.question: Zebra

quests.instruction: This bird stays awake at night and can turn its head almost all the way round. Which bird?
quests.hint: Its big eyes help it find food when there is little light.
quests.explanation: Owls hunt at night. Their necks are so flexible that they can look behind them without moving their bodies.
quests.funFact: An owl's feathers are soft at the edges, so its wings make hardly any sound.
quests.question: Owl

quests.instruction: Just before sunrise, a loud call rings across the farmyard. Who is crowing?
quests.hint: He has a bright red crest on top of his head.
quests.explanation: Roosters crow at dawn, but they also crow at other times to tell nearby roosters, "This is my patch."
quests.funFact: A rooster's red head crest is called a comb, and it helps him lose extra heat on warm days.
quests.question: Rooster

quests.instruction: Which bird has a flat bill and webbed feet that work like little paddles?
quests.hint: Its feet have skin stretched between the toes.
quests.explanation: Webbed feet push against the water like paddles, so a duck can swim along easily.
quests.funFact: A duck spreads oil from near its tail over its feathers, so rain rolls right off.
quests.question: Duck

quests.instruction: Name the sea animal that has eight long arms covered in suckers.
quests.hint: It has no hard bones, so it can squeeze through very small gaps.
quests.explanation: An octopus has eight arms and a soft body. It can squeeze through any hole big enough for its beak.
quests.funFact: An octopus has three hearts.
quests.question: Octopus

quests.instruction: Name the sea animal that leaps out of the water and whistles to its friends.
quests.hint: Even though it lives in the sea, it has to come up to breathe air.
quests.explanation: Dolphins use whistles and clicks to talk to each other. They are mammals, so they surface to breathe.
quests.funFact: A dolphin sleeps with one half of its brain awake, so it can keep surfacing for air.
quests.question: Dolphin

quests.instruction: Which sea creature scuttles sideways across the sand?
quests.hint: It has two pinching claws and a hard shell.
quests.explanation: Most crabs walk sideways because of the way their leg joints bend.
quests.funFact: A crab grows by shedding its hard outer shell and growing a new, bigger one.
quests.question: Crab

quests.instruction: Which small animal turns the sweet nectar from flowers into honey?
quests.hint: It carries its sweet harvest back to a busy hive.
quests.explanation: Honey bees collect nectar and carry it back to the hive, where it is turned into honey.
quests.funFact: One bee makes only about one-twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in her whole life.
quests.question: Bee

quests.instruction: Pick the insect that starts out as a caterpillar and later grows colourful wings.
quests.hint: It changes shape completely as it grows up.
quests.explanation: A butterfly begins as an egg, then a caterpillar. The caterpillar wraps itself in a chrysalis and comes out with wings.
quests.funFact: Butterflies taste with their feet, so they can tell right away whether a leaf is a good place to lay eggs.
quests.question: Butterfly

quests.instruction: A long line of tiny workers carries crumbs across the ground. Which insects are they?
quests.hint: They follow each other along a trail of scent.
quests.explanation: Ants leave scent trails so other ants can find the food. That is why they march in lines.
quests.funFact: An ant can carry things many times heavier than its own body.
quests.question: Ant

quests.instruction: Pick the animal that swings through trees and holds fruit in its hands.
quests.hint: It grips branches with both its hands and its feet.
quests.explanation: Monkeys have nimble fingers and toes that grip branches, and many of them eat fruit.
quests.funFact: Some capuchin monkeys crack nuts open using stones.
quests.question: Monkey

quests.instruction: Only the boys of this big cat wear a thick, fluffy collar of hair. Which cat?
quests.hint: The fluffy collar is called a mane.
quests.explanation: Male lions grow manes, and female lions don't. Lions are also the only big cats that live in groups.
quests.funFact: A lion can nap for around twenty hours on a lazy day.
quests.question: Lion

quests.instruction: Which black-and-white animal spends most of its day munching bamboo?
quests.hint: Its favourite meal grows in tall green stalks.
quests.explanation: Giant pandas eat mostly bamboo, and they spend more than ten hours a day chewing it.
quests.funFact: A baby panda is tiny and pink when it is born, and smaller than a stick of butter.
quests.question: Panda

quests.instruction: Which bird cannot fly, but swims fast through icy water?
quests.hint: Its wings work like flippers.
quests.explanation: Penguins swim with flipper-shaped wings. Their smooth feathers and thick fat keep them warm in cold seas.
quests.funFact: Father emperor penguins balance an egg on their feet to keep it warm through the Antarctic winter.
quests.question: Penguin

quests.instruction: A sandy land, very little water, and an animal with a big lump on its back. Which animal?
quests.hint: The lump stores something the animal can use when food is hard to find.
quests.explanation: A camel's hump is filled with fat, which it can use for energy when it can't find food.
quests.funFact: Camels have long, thick eyelashes that keep blowing sand out of their eyes.
quests.question: Camel

quests.instruction: Which animal hops on big back legs and carries its baby in a pouch?
quests.hint: Its baby is tiny when it's born and spends months snuggled in a pocket.
quests.explanation: A baby kangaroo, called a joey, finishes growing safely inside its mother's pouch.
quests.funFact: A kangaroo's strong tail helps it balance when it hops.
quests.question: Kangaroo

quests.instruction: Find the animal that has no legs and slithers across the ground.
quests.hint: It moves by squeezing its muscles in waves along its body.
quests.explanation: Snakes slither without legs. Their bodies push against the ground in waves.
quests.funFact: A snake flicks its tongue to pick up smells from the air.
quests.question: Snake

quests.instruction: Find the animal that can pull its head and legs inside a hard shell.
quests.hint: Its shell is joined to its bones and can't be taken off.
quests.explanation: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton, so it is a built-in shelter it can carry anywhere.
quests.funFact: Many turtles can live for more than fifty years.
quests.question: Turtle

quests.instruction: Name the green animal that has long back legs for jumping and croaks near ponds.
quests.hint: It uses a sticky tongue to catch flies.
quests.explanation: Frogs use their strong back legs to leap, and they spend a lot of time near water.
quests.funFact: Frogs don't drink through their mouths. They soak up water through their skin.
quests.question: Frog

quests.instruction: Spot the farm animal that rolls in muddy puddles to cool off.
quests.hint: It can't sweat very much, so it has to find another way to stay cool.
quests.explanation: Pigs have very few sweat glands, so a muddy wallow cools them down. The mud also protects their skin from the sun.
quests.funFact: Pigs are among the smartest farm animals, and they can learn simple tricks.
quests.question: Pig

quests.instruction: Find the bright bird that can copy the sounds that people make.
quests.hint: It is a colourful bird that loves to join in the conversation.
quests.explanation: Parrots are very good at copying sounds, including human words, which they learn by listening.
quests.funFact: Many parrots hold their food in one foot while they eat, like a hand.
quests.question: Parrot

quests.instruction: Name the wild cat that has orange fur with dark stripes.
quests.hint: It is the biggest of all the big cats.
quests.explanation: Tiger stripes help it blend into tall grass and shadows when it is sneaking up on food.
quests.funFact: Unlike many cats, tigers often enjoy swimming.
quests.question: Tiger
